Procedure: Attended, full-night diagnostic polysomnography.

Palms and soles are clear of any lesions. Sclerae are anicteric.

Clinical History: 29-year-old female with a known history of Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), presenting with new-onset proteinuria and hematuria. Biopsy is performed to evaluate for lupus nephritis.

Diagnosis: Kidney, native, biopsy: Lupus Nephritis, Class IV-G(A)

Light Microscopy Description: The specimen consists of two cores of renal cortex and medulla. Up to 28 glomeruli are identified for evaluation. All glomeruli show global, diffuse endocapillary and mesangial/hypercellularity with neutrophilic infiltration. Multiple glomeruli contain wire loop lesions. There is moderate tubular atrophy and interstitial fibrosis involving approximately 30% of the cortex. No crescents or fibrinoid necrosis are seen.

Immunofluorescence Description:
IgG+: 3+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops (full house pattern).
IgA: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.
IgM: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.
C3: 3+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.
C1q: 2+ granular staining in mesangium and capillary loops.
Fibrinogen: Negative.
Albumin: Negative.

Electron Microscopy Description: Electron microscopy confirms diffuse subendothelial and mesangial electron-dense deposits. Tubuloreticular inclusions are present within endothelial cells.
There is approximately 50% podocyte foot process effacement.

Comment: The combined findings are diagnostic of active, diffuse global lupus nephritis, ISN/RPS

Specimen: Native kidney biopsy

Clinical History: 25-year-old female with a one-month history of night sweats. Concern for lymphoma.

Gross Description: Received fresh, labeled left neck mass is an encapsulated lymph node measuring 2.8 x 2.1 x 1.5 cm. The cut surface is tan white and firm, with a vaguely nodular appearance.

Microscopic Description: Sections of the lymph node show complete effacement of the normal architecture by a nodular infiltrate. The nodules are defined by broad bands of collagenous fibrosis. Within the nodules, there is a mixed inflammation background composed of small lymphocytes, classic binucleated Reed-Sternberg cells and their mononuclear variants (Hodgkin cells). These cells have large vesicular nuclei, prominent eosinophilic nucleoli, and abundant cytoplasm.

Immunohistochemistry: The large, atypical cells show the following immunophenotype:
CD15: Positive
PDX5: Positive (dim)
CD45: Negative
CD20: Negative
CD3: Highlights the background T-cell population.
Comment: The morphologic findings in conjunction with the immunophenotype (CD30+, CD15+, PAX5+, CD45+) are diagnostic of Classical Hodgkin Lymphoma, Nodular Sclerosis subtype. Clinical correlation and appropriate oncologic management are recommended.

Specimen: Left cervical lymph node

Report status: Final

The patient is a 22-year-old male who presented for a routine skin examination.
He noted a mole on his upper back that he believes has become slightly darker
over the past year. He denies any symptoms of pain or itching associated with the
lesion. He has a history of significant sun exposure during his teen years and
reports occasional sunburns.
PROCEDURES:
Shave Biopsy Upper Back: A 5mm pigmented macule was identified on the
superior aspect of the right scapula. After obtaining consent, the area was
anesthetized with 1% lidocaine with epinephrine and a deep shave biopsy of the
lesion was performed. Hemostasis was achieved with aluminum chloride. The
specimen was sent for histopathologic examination.
IMPRESSION:
MICROSCOPIC DESCRIPTION: Sections show a symmetric, well-circumscribed
proliferation of nested and single melanocytes confined to the dermal-epidermal
junction. The melanocytes are uniform in size and shape with no significant
cytologic atypia. No mitotic activity or ulceration is identified.
DIAGNOSIS: Junctional melanocytic nevus, benign.
